clusters.text: Maryland Democrat challenges party leader after midterms sweep, saying: ‘The American people called for change’ Chris Van Hollen, the Democratic senator of Maryland, announced on Thursday that he is challenging Chuck Schumer for the role of Senate majority leader when Democrats regain the chamber’s majority in January. “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies – but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement posted on social media. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.” Schumer, the leader of the Democratic minority in the current Senate, responded less than a minute later in a social media post of his own. “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” Schumer wrote. “I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together – 55 seats and counting is an amazing result – and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.” The battle pits a progressive Democrat, Van Hollen, against a centrist, Schumer. Van Hollen’s challenge comes after he said he was considering a bid and after Schumer said he had the necessary support to win. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December. The race will be the first contested election for Democratic leader in decades. The question of whether to re-elect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators will not say publicly how they will vote. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election, and Schumer recruited many of the party’s winning candidates and raised money for them. But some of the winning candidates, most notably Michigan’s senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, did not initially have Schumer’s support. Schumer has been talking to Democratic senators since the election about forming an agenda for 2027. “I’m going to win it,” Schumer told the Associated Press in an interview last week.

The timeline for his return ought to be an open question at this point, as their press release mentions that he’ll be reevaluated in two (2) weeks. That tracks with the reporting last night that he felt a pain he had never felt before. This type of injury can be overcome without the need for surgery, but in that scenario, it’s usually a 3-4 week timeline for recovery… if it’s closer to a strain. But this is being described as a “tear,” which could very easily mean a couple of months recovery time. There’s a lot of fast and twisting upper body motion needed to get an open shot or disrupt a passing lane. It was only a couple of days ago that the Warriors lost Steph’s backup to a hamstring strain, so the injury picture has grown from outsized to overwhelming. Steph, Brandon Williams, Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, Gary Payton II, Will Richard, Kristaps Porzingis — it’s not as though Golden State had All-Star backups or were the deepest team in the association heading into the season, but there’s “testing a team’s depth” and there’s “Oops! All injured,” and, folks, we’re here. There’s no making up for Curry’s ~28 a night and clutch shots, but if there is one throughline through this weird start to a season it’s that rotations have had a pretty solid flow to them in spite of the injuries. As Draymond put it last night: > “The spirit of this team is better,” Green said. “We’re more certain of who we are, what makes us a good team. I think that puts us in a better position to be successful without him as opposed to where we were last year. Then obviously [Yaxel Lendeborg], having a guy you can give the ball to and he can create an advantage. [Brandin Podziemski] is playing a lot better. ... It puts us in a better position.” This isn’t to suggest that Yaxel & Pods will each score 40 a night and everyone else who’s left will step up, but this puzzle that the team had been working hard to piece together already just has to keep up that effort and see what shakes out. Hopefully, the Warriors are able to weather this surprise storm until Steph Curry returns.

clusters.text: The first Gemini smartglasses are a collab between Google, Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker. Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at “ intelligent eyewear ” for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. That will also determine the final pricing. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses. The setup here is similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses we’ve seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet. In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier". Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias. He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. clusters.title: Where does Kane rank among all-time England greats?
clusters.snippet: Harry Kane is England's all-time top scorer and record appearance maker, but where does he rank among the Three Lions' greatest players?
clusters.text: Harry Kane is now England's most-capped men's player as well as his country's record goalscorer, but harder to quantify is where these achievements place him among the Three Lions' greatest ever players. This is a tricky debate with so many variables and a timescale as old as the game itself and, to my mind, not merely a determination of a player's individual ability but also a measure of their impact upon the nation's psyche. Ballon d'Or winners Stanley Matthews, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen would surely have a shout if the criteria was such, not to mention genius technicians such as Glenn Hoddle, Chris Waddle and John Barnes. Likewise, if any England boss managed to extract the best from Paul Scholes, Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard they would be surely making a classic late dart from midfield. But to qualify as one of the greatest England players of all time, you need the above ability combined with an impactful overall contribution - those memorable moments and an element of longevity - in a Three Lions shirt. It might be controversial then to leave out Geoff Hurst, who produced the most recognisable performance in England history, while the man he replaced, Jimmy Greaves, would be a shoo-in were it not for injury earlier in the tournament. It is also hard to rank the contribution of those whose best football came outside of major tournaments and before the dawn of continental competitions - see Eddie Hapgood, Tom Finney, Nat Lofthouse, Dixie Dean et al. Spice Boy. Celebrity. Galactico. There is no argument David Beckham is one of the most iconic England players of all time, but he backed it up on the pitch, too. Beckham was the face of the Three Lions for a generation, and to his credit managed to overcome the vicious fallout of his red card against Argentina in 1998. At times he seemed to single-handedly carry England, most notably scoring a 93rd-minute free-kick against Greece to qualify for the 2002 World Cup. Beckham's former team-mate Gary Neville called him the "most influential player out of England in transforming football". It's true. clusters.text: Ranchi: A door-to-door survey would be conducted across Ranchi district from Nov 20 to Jan 10, 2027 to update the ‘Shishu Panji’ (child register) so as to track the school enrolment status of children, aged between three and 18 years.Acting on the directions of the Jharkhand Education Project Council (JEPC), the exercise seeks to identify out-of-school children, including dropouts and those never enrolled, to ensure their admission in the upcoming academic session.The drive’s first phase, habitation mapping, was originally scheduled to conclude by Nov 10 to pave the way for the household survey. clusters.title: MP pushes for AIIMS-like institution in Prayagraj
clusters.text: Highlighting the lack of adequate medical infrastructure in Prayagraj, Allahabad MP Ujjwal Raman Singh on Tuesday said the city urgently needed an AIIMS-like institution, as patients were still forced to travel to Lucknow or Delhi for advanced and life-saving treatment. Speaking at the inauguration of newly installed medical equipment at Swaroop Rani Nehru (SRN) Hospital (affiliated to the Motilal Nehru Medical College), the MP said the provision of ventilators and dialysis machines through the Central Warehousing Corporation’s (CWC) corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative would strengthen treatment facilities for critically ill patients. Under the initiative, ₹2 crore was sanctioned for Motilal Nehru Medical College, while ventilators worth ₹2.5 crore were provided to Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGIMS). The MP said strengthening public healthcare facilities was essential to ensure that economically weaker patients could access advanced treatment without having to travel to other cities. MP representative Vinay Kushwaha recalled that Motilal Nehru Medical College was established in 1961 by then Uttar Pradesh chief minister Chandra Bhanu Gupta. He said former MP Kunwar Rewati Raman Singh had played a key role in securing ₹125 crore from the Centre during the Manmohan Singh-led government, when Ghulam Nabi Azad was the Union health minister. The then chief minister, Akhilesh Yadav had subsequently contributed ₹25 crore towards developing the college’s super-specialty hospital. Kushwaha said affordable treatment at government hospitals provided significant relief to the poor. Citing the example of a stent procedure, he said it costs around ₹65,000 at the hospital, compared to ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh at private hospitals. MLNMC principal Dr AK Verma, CWC HR head Prakash Chandra Rai, chief medical superintendent Dr Neelma Singh, Dr Mohit Jain, Dr Arvind Gupta, Dr Anil Singh, Dr Santosh Maurya and MP representative Vinay Kushwaha were among those present.
